task.description: Write test spec + test code for REQ-060's gate-approved PinRebind implementation (SECURITY-REVIEWER and REVIEWER both PASSed lib/letflow/engine/pin_rebind.ex). Cover all 6 REQ-060 acceptance criteria from docs/requirements.yaml, and register 'INSTANCE_PINS_REBOUND' in test fixtures per ISS-0071/GH#257 (REVIEWER's finding this run: EventStore.append/2 rejects unregistered event types, and no production code registers TASK_COMPLETED/INSTANCE_CANCELLED/INSTANCE_PINS_REBOUND -- test fixtures must self-register, mirroring engine_cancel_instance_test.exs's established pattern).
acceptance_criteria: AC1: valid rebind appends exactly one INSTANCE_PINS_REBOUND event with correct payload shape; a no-op entry (requested version == current) contributes no payload entry
AC2: UnknownPinRef rejects the WHOLE request (zero writes) even when other entries in the same request are individually valid -- verified by reading the effective pin set back unchanged
AC3: InstanceNotRebindable for all three terminal statuses (COMPLETED, CANCELLED, ERROR) tested individually
AC4: missing/empty reason, empty entries list, and malformed entry each return a distinct invalid-input error
AC5: post-rebind, REQ-059's effective pin set reflects new versions AND reconstruction derives the same set from INSTANCE_STARTED + INSTANCE_PINS_REBOUND with zero catalog reads
AC6: lock contention surfaces as ConcurrentModification rather than blocking (a real concurrent-transaction test), and moduledoc states ERROR is the terminal status meant by PIN-05's 'FAILED' text
Test code compiles cleanly (mix compile --force, mix test --no-start compile-check)

result.summary:
Wrote test/specs/REQ-060.md (17 numbered test cases mapped to all 6 REQ-060 ACs, a coverage-summary table, and an explicit 'Pin fixture strategy' section explaining why every fixture rebinds the always-present :variable_schema pin rather than :catalog_entry/:module -- Letflow.Definitions.Graph has no dispatchable SERVICE_TASK/SUB_PROCESS implementation yet, so a catalog/module pin can never survive a real Engine.create/2 call through the public pipeline, matching REQ-059's own already-documented gap at engine_test.exs:1006-1020) and one test file, test/letflow/engine/pin_rebind_test.exs (27 tests across 6 describe blocks matching the AC groupings).

Event-type registration: provisioned_tenant/0 registers 'INSTANCE_PINS_REBOUND', 'INSTANCE_CANCELLED' (needed for the AC3 CANCELLED fixture, via Engine.cancel_instance/3) and 'EXECUTION_ERROR' (needed for the AC3 ERROR fixture, via Engine.set_instance_error/2) itself, exactly mirroring engine_cancel_instance_test.exs:63-97's register_event_type!/2 pattern per ISS-0071/GH#257's finding -- 'INSTANCE_STARTED' needs no explicit registration (auto-seeded by TenantProvisioning.replay_migrations/2).

AC1: one test appends a single changed entry and reads the raw INSTANCE_PINS_REBOUND event payload back via Reconstruction.read_full_log/3 (not just the return value) to confirm entries/actor/reason shape; a second test proves a no-op entry (version already matches) still commits exactly one event but with an empty payload entries list, distinguishing 'per-entry omission' from 'whole rebind skipped'.

AC2: one test orders a genuinely-valid entry BEFORE an unknown-ref entry (proving a full pre-pass, not partial commit-as-you-go), asserts {:error, {:unknown_pin_ref, :catalog_entry, ref}}, then reads PinResolver.reconstruct_effective_pins/2 back to confirm the valid entry's ref is still at its ORIGINAL version, and confirms zero INSTANCE_PINS_REBOUND events were ever appended.

AC3: three independent tests, one per terminal status -- COMPLETED via a START->END graph that completes inside Engine.create/2 itself, CANCELLED via a real Engine.cancel_instance/3 call, ERROR via a real Engine.set_instance_error/2 call -- deliberately NOT parameterized into one test, since check_rebind_eligibility/1 is REVIEWER-confirmed to be a hand-written three-way case rather than a reuse of InstanceProjection.terminal?/1 (which excludes :error), so each status needs its own independently-failing test to catch a regression back to terminal?/1's narrower set.

AC4: six tests -- missing :reason key and empty/whitespace-only :reason both assert the SAME {:error, :invalid_reason} (closing the 'missing vs empty is one condition' half of the design), missing :entries key and empty [] both assert the SAME {:error, :empty_entries}, and two malformed-entry tests (missing :version key -> {:malformed_entry, 0, :missing_or_unexpected_keys}; invalid :kind value -> {:malformed_entry, 0, {:invalid_kind, "bogus"}}) prove :malformed_entry itself carries distinctly-shaped reasons, not one hardcoded atom.

AC5: one test confirms reconstruct_effective_pins/2 shows the new version post-rebind; a second test independently hand-derives the same result by reading INSTANCE_STARTED + INSTANCE_PINS_REBOUND directly via Reconstruction.read_full_log/3 and calling PinResolver.merge_effective_pins/2 manually, then asserts equality with reconstruct_effective_pins/2's own result -- demonstrating the effective set really is a pure fold over exactly those two event types; a third test proves the 'zero catalog reads' half structurally: rebind_attrs() has no :pin_lookup field at all (unlike Engine.create/2's attrs[:pin_lookup]), demonstrated by supplying a call-counted fake :pin_lookup key in attrs and confirming it is never invoked (0 calls) because rebind_pins/3's own code never reads that key.

AC6: one genuine two-Task.async-process concurrency test mirroring test/letflow/engine/reconstruction_test.exs's with_locked_projection/3 exactly -- a real second Postgres connection holds a plain FOR UPDATE lock on the instance_projections row (Sandbox mode :auto, real separate connections, not sandbox-serialized), then rebind_pins/3 is called against the same instance and asserted to return {:error, {:concurrent_modification, instance_id}} promptly (:timer.tc-measured, asserted under 2s against the lock holder's own 5s hold budget, as the 'rather than blocking' half of the claim), with the row's variables/current_nodes confirmed unchanged and zero INSTANCE_PINS_REBOUND events appended afterwards. A second test does a whitespace-normalized moduledoc substring check (mirroring engine_test.exs's own normalized_moduledoc/1 idiom) confirming the moduledoc's exact 'FAILED'/'ERROR is the status PIN-05's text means'/'terminal for rebind purposes specifically' wording survives verbatim.

Compile-checked per instructions (did NOT run mix test for pass/fail -- that is TEST-RUNNER's job): mix compile --force is clean (79 files, no warnings/errors); mix test --no-start test/letflow/engine/pin_rebind_test.exs compiles the test file cleanly (the only errors shown are the expected --no-start Ecto-repo-not-started errors from test_helper.exs's TenantSchemaReaper, unrelated to this file, identical to what any other test file would show under --no-start). No wall-clock or unseeded-randomness dependency (Ecto.UUID.generate()/System.unique_integer/1 for fixture uniqueness only, matching every sibling test file's convention).
